name: Batad Village Proper
description: The heart of it all, where clustered homestays sit right within the natural bowl of hand-built rice terraces. You wake to sculpted green slopes on every side, walk stone paths between farms, and share family dinners. Rustic, unforgettable, and completely car-free.
bestFor: Culture seekers and slow travelers who want to live inside the landscape
pros: Unmatched terrace views from your doorstep
cons: Basic amenities and weak or no wifi
Reached only on foot down from the saddle

name: The Saddle Viewpoint
tagline: Where the road ends and the walk begins
description: The ridge where the rough access road from Banaue stops and the footpath down to the village starts. A cluster of simple viewpoint stops and a few basic rooms sit here, offering a first sweeping panorama of the amphitheater before you descend on foot.
bestFor: Arrivals wanting a first view and a shorter carry to the village
pros: First dramatic overlook of the terraces
Slightly easier access than the village floor
cons: Still a real walk down to homestays

name: Tappiya Falls Side
tagline: Down the trail to the thundering falls
description: The lower reaches beyond the village, where a steep trail leads across terraces and down to powerful Tappiya Falls. There is no lodging here, but it is the trekking highlight of the area, a rewarding half-day hike best done with a local guide from the village.
bestFor: Trekkers and nature lovers chasing waterfalls and raw scenery
pros: Refreshing swim spot on hot days
cons: Steep, slippery descent and climb back
No facilities, so bring water and a guide

name: Banaue Town
description: The nearest town and the practical hub for the whole area, with inns, restaurants, shops, ATMs, and the best mobile signal and power around. This is where night buses from Manila arrive and where tricycles set off for the Batad saddle. A comfortable base for supplies and connectivity.
bestFor: Travelers needing wifi, supplies, ATMs, or a comfortable staging point
pros: Most reliable signal, power, and services
cons: Not the terraces themselves, a rough ride away
Busier and less immersive than Batad
